scope: Editor decoration async completion must apply only to the page/edit session selected before access approval. Preserve valid same-target edits and inline panel reuse.

findings.before: Decoration insertion awaited access, then its parent callback read the current editor/page. In a still-mounted panel, a page change or resetForCreate during approval inserted the old selection into that different page/new draft and closed the panel. The new draft intentionally reused cover_page, so matching only a page ID would not be sufficient.
findings.evidence: Two controlled tests using the actual editor view model, real decoration panel and a delayed access gate failed before the fix: changed page and changed draft. Valid same-page edits, page changes before the tap, and closing before approval already passed.
fix: DecorateStickerTab optionally captures a lightweight approval guard at selection time, before its access await. Check it before changing the selected decoration or invoking the insertion callback.

DecoratePanel supplies the guard, checking notifier identity, editSessionIdentity, current page ID and editing album ID. Capture occurs per tap, so intentionally changing the page before choosing a material still works.

Keep the existing finally-based single-flight lock release, including a rejected stale approval. Standalone catalog previews need no editor provider or guard. No ownership/server access check is bypassed.

findings.before: The old _Interaction mock in the artwork-name/thumbnail fixture did not implement sortByZ. The current layer panel called it and received null instead of a layer list. This failure was unrelated to the async insertion change.
findings.fix: Use a real read-only LayerInteractionManager.printPreview for that fixture and dispose it at teardown; retain the existing rendering-only mocks in other tests.

initial_fixture_attempt.classification: Two reproduced target failures plus one invalid replacement fixture. That fixture called invalidate on a real notifier, rerunning its build/late-final initialization rather than replacing its instance. Removed that fixture, and made no production change on its basis. No production invalidate/refresh call for this notifier was found in the scoped search.

controlled_baseline.classification: Intentional before-fix reproduction for page and reused-ID draft changes; three valid/lifecycle behaviors pass.

first_related.classification: All new target cases passed after the production fix; the remaining failure was the old null-sort test mock subsequently repaired.

new_cases: Changed page during delayed approval does not insert or close the panel.
New draft during delayed approval does not insert despite reusing the same page ID.
Rejected stale approval releases the lock and a fresh selection can apply exactly once.
Edits to layers on the same target survive and do not cancel valid insertion; duplicate taps remain single flight.
A still-mounted inline panel captures the target at material selection, preserving page changes before the tap.
Closing while access is pending never inserts, closes again or leaves transient callbacks.
verification.scoped_git_diff_check: passed; source/test trailing whitespace also checked

resources.handling: One test process at a time with concurrency=1. No other Flutter test process observed in prelaunch checks. Regenerated the missing test asset bundle in the initial test run, then reused it with --no-test-assets. No user/shared caches or other tasks were stopped/deleted.

verification.external_effects: No app build/device run, deployment, operational database access or customer data mutation.

checked: The guard is captured once per user selection, not during list building, scrolling or thumbnail decoding. It holds only notifier/session/scalar target references for the existing single pending operation.
No new cache, listener, timer, worker, image decode, document copy or background task is added. The existing insertion lock still releases in finally.
A disposed tab short-circuits before consulting the parent guard; a changed notifier short-circuits before accessing the old editor target.
The guard compares target identity instead of layer revision, preserving content edits to the same page. The callback still uses fresh current layers and computes the existing canvas size.
Stale approval changes neither selected material state nor target layers and does not close the tool. A subsequent valid tap remains usable.

Existing paid/free/cancel/duplicate/disposal gating, frame and phrase pickers, undo/reorder, more-menu dialog handoff, responsive material picker cases and actual material artwork consistency regressions pass.
Default point-shop access/purchase logic, prices, ownership, saved document format, material keys, cover artwork, main/store layout and existing photo/cache behavior are unchanged.
review.shared_workspace: Preserved all prior dirty workspace changes. Wrote only the listed files and this new run evidence/report.

next_candidates: Review page insertion/deletion/reordering and stable target-ID handling before extending asynchronous target guards to other editor tools; reproduce a concrete failure before editing.
Review pending phrase/frame application at their editor caller boundaries with the same target-change cases, while preserving current gate and route-close guards.
Continue main/store/reader hidden-resume checks against the newest verification records rather than repeating the completed shelf/controller changes.

limits: The controlled fixture uses a delayed access gate and local fake services with the real editor VM/panel. It does not execute a real payment, authentication change or production server request.
The fix prevents stale application; it does not cancel an already submitted purchase. Existing server-confirmed material ownership and purchase behavior remain authoritative.

No physical-device FPS, peak native/app memory, heap snapshot or device leak profile was measured. Constant-size target checks and absence of new background/cached work are code-review properties, not measured performance guarantees.
Target checks retain the existing page/session identity model. Exhaustive page-ID reuse during every insertion/deletion/undo sequence is not claimed by these six cases.
